notable_absence.finding: The registry promotes index:standard-storage AND index:memory-optimized-storage, and offersConfigurationChoice exists as a promoted predicate to join them - the server tree offers the choice. This page, which is the Capella page for that subject and is still filed at the filename storage-modes.md, has no such relation because it has no such choice: 'memory-optimized' does not appear once, and neither do Forestdb or Nitro. Capella collapses the axis to a single member and then stops calling it an axis. Two further absences worth phase 2's attention. (1) The word 'mode' never appears on this page - not in the H1 ('Index Storage Settings'), not in the anchor (#standard-index-storage), not in the body. The only place 'modes' survives is the filename. (2) The page states no configurability at all: no setting name, no default value other than the Bloom filter's 'enabled', no API, no UI path, and 'Compaction is handled automatically'. For a page titled 'Settings' there is nothing a reader can set.

cross_component_finding: Three things. (1) This page and query-without-index.md, two files apart in the same directory, disagree about Memory-only buckets: here 'Couchbase Capella index storage supports indexes for both Couchbase buckets and Memory-only buckets', there sequential scans are unsupported on them. Both can be literally true (an index is not a sequential scan) but the pair will read as a contradiction to anyone skimming, and phase 2 should keep the two supportsBucketType / doesNotSupport relations adjacent so the distinction stays visible. (2) The page carries three different names for its own subject - filename 'storage-modes', H1 and link text 'Index Storage Settings', section heading 'Index Storage', anchor '#standard-index-storage' - and indexing-overview.md links to it as 'Index Storage Settings'. Four spellings, one page. (3) 'Plasma is highly scalable and performant storage engine' is missing an article ('a highly scalable'), a copy defect in the sentence that is the page's only characterisation of the engine.
cross_product_finding: This page settles, for Capella, the question of whether 'storage engine' and 'storage mode' are the same thing - and it settles it by keeping them at two levels while removing the choice at the upper one. An index HAS a storage setting (standard index storage), and that setting IS SUPPORTED BY an engine (Plasma): 'Standard index-storage is supported by the Plasma storage engine.' So they are not synonyms. But because Capella ships exactly one member of the upper level, the two collapse in practice into one sentence - 'All indexes in Couchbase Capella use the Couchbase Plasma storage engine' - and the page then drops the upper level's own vocabulary ('mode') entirely. The server tree keeps both levels populated: two promoted storage concepts, a promoted offersConfigurationChoice predicate, plus couchstore and magma as promoted engines for the Data Service. Note the asymmetry that leaves: the registry has engines for data storage (couchstore, magma) but had none for index storage until this record minted storage-engine:plasma, even though Plasma is the only engine any Capella index can use. Whoever promoted couchstore and magma was reading Data Service pages, and nobody had yet read this one.
